title: Expose model metadata + release notes endpoints (typed models + pagination helpers)
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
Summary: This PR adds Python SDK support for querying model metadata (schema v1) and customer-visible model release notes/change history. It introduces typed response models, a small pagination utility for cursor-based endpoints, and minimal documentation/examples.

Motivation: Console + docs are adding model change history and release notes generated from registry/control-plane events. Support and customers also want programmatic access (e.g., validate pinned versions, detect deprecations, audit what changed during a rollout). This SDK work unblocks early adopters and reduces support burden for "silent change" escalations.

What’s included: (1) New client surfaces: client.model_metadata.get(model_id=..., version=..., deployment=...) and client.release_notes.list(model_id=..., deployment=..., severity=..., since=..., page_size=...). (2) Typed models for ModelMetadataV1, Compatibility, DeploymentAvailability, Deprecation, and ReleaseNoteEntry. (3) Pagination helpers: a small CursorPage[T] container and iter_pages()/iter_all() helpers that work with Redwood’s next_cursor responses. (4) Redaction-aware behavior: the SDK only exposes public fields returned by the API; internal-only fields are not modeled and are ignored if present (defensive). (5) Tests for pagination and JSON parsing; basic docs in README + generated reference stubs.

API endpoints used (already live behind feature flag in control plane): GET /v1/models/{model_id}/metadata?version=...&deployment=... and GET /v1/release-notes?model_id=...&deployment=...&cursor=...&limit=...

Notes: The models intentionally treat unknown fields as allowed to reduce churn as schema evolves (we rely on explicit typed access for stable fields). This matches the v1 metadata schema guidelines.

Rollout: Safe to ship as additive SDK release. No behavior changes to existing endpoints. After merge, we will cut v0.18.0 of redwood-sdk-python and update the Console/docs integration examples to reference these APIs.
commits: Expose model metadata + release notes client methods
Add typed models for model metadata schema v1 + release notes entries
Docs: README usage examples + reference updates
Fix: handle null/absent deprecation fields; tighten type hints
conversation: Quentin Harris (review): Can we align naming with registry docs? I’d prefer ModelMetadata (not ModelMeta) and version should be semver string. Also please confirm we’re not modeling internal-only notes fields.

Sahana Iyer (author): Updated naming to ModelMetadataV1 to match schema doc; version is str and passed through (no semver parsing). Internal-only fields are not included in models; additionally set extra='ignore' so if backend accidentally includes internal fields, we drop them.

Jada Williams (review): Pagination helper looks good. Suggest adding iter_all() with a hard cap / max_pages to avoid infinite loops if cursor repeats. Also please add an idempotency test for repeated next_cursor.
Sahana Iyer (author): Added max_pages default=1000 and a guard that raises PaginationError if next_cursor repeats. Added unit test covering repeated cursor scenario.
Chloe Martin (review): For release_notes.list(), can we support deployment filter values (hosted|dedicated|private) and leave room for region? Customers keep asking "what changed in my environment".

Sahana Iyer (author): Added Deployment enum (hosted/dedicated/private) and pass-through query param. Region is not yet supported by the endpoint; left an optional region param on the method that raises ValueError until backend supports it (keeps signature stable without silently ignoring).

Connor O'Brien (review): Please ensure CHANGELOG notes mention this is additive + gated by backend availability. Also would like a minimal example that shows how to fetch release notes for a pinned model version.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated CHANGELOG and README with example: retrieve metadata for model_id + version, then query release notes with since timestamp and filter by severity.
Jada Williams (approval): Approved. Thanks for adding the cursor-repeat guard; we hit that exact bug in an early internal API draft.
Quentin Harris (approval): LGTM after naming updates.
